clue.text: Unqualified to travel in arctic, go round east

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round, enclosing, the abbreviation for east
the letters of arctic and go travel about, ending up in a fresh order

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Someone without training is told to go on an Arctic expedition, circling to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to travel in' scrambles the letters, giving CATGORIC, and 'round' wraps that about the E. 'Unqualified' suggests untrained, but here it means absolute.
explanation.definitionFit: An unqualified statement is absolute and without reservations, just as a categoric one is.

clue.text: African city lacks own family of kings

indicators.note: the city name goes without the letters of the word own, so they are removed

parts.note: Cape Town is the South African port city
taken as written

explanation.surface: A city in Africa is short of a royal family of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' strips OWN from CAPE TOWN. Hugh Capet founded the Capetian dynasty of French kings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Capets were the dynasty of French monarchs descended from Hugh Capet, a royal house.

clue.text: Stole something left inside: all one needed for the job?

definitions.text: all one needed for the job?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left goes within the phrase meaning stole something

parts.note: to steal something is to take it, giving 'took it'

explanation.surface: A thief pocketed something and left it inside: everything needed for the heist?
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts L within TOOK IT. The question mark marks the definition as a loose description: a kit holds the tools for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A kit of tools is the full set of implements a tradesman carries to do a particular piece of work.

clue.text: One giving creeps right to hold up play

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first, propping it up

parts.note: Ghosts is Ibsen's play
a Tory is on the political right

explanation.surface: A right-winger tries to delay a theatre production that gives people the creeps.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'to hold up' puts TORY under GHOSTS, supporting it. 'creeps' here means the shivers of fear.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale of spooks and hauntings is told to give listeners the shivers.

clue.text: Collector of words I acknowledge has new base

indicators.note: the word for I acknowledge gets a fresh letter at its foot in place of its final one

parts.note: Roger is the radio reply meaning message received
T stands for thymine, one of the bases in DNA

explanation.surface: Someone admits a word collector has moved to a different headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has new' swaps the final R of ROGER for T, the chemist's symbol for the DNA base thymine. Peter Mark Roget compiled the famous Thesaurus.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Mark Roget gathered synonyms into his celebrated Thesaurus of English words and phrases.

clue.text: Father's day?

parts.note: not the June celebration of dads but the festive day belonging to the gift-bringing Father of folklore in red

explanation.surface: A question about the day set aside to honour dads.
explanation.walkthrough: Father's Day is the obvious reading; Father here is the bearded gift-bringer of 25 December.
explanation.definitionFit: December 25 is the occasion most associated with the jolly gift-giving figure called Father.

clue.text: Not quite succeed in army course

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to pass an exam is to succeed
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A recruit nearly gets through an army training course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last S of PASS. 'course' is a course of a meal, not a training course.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of noodles or spaghetti is served as one part of a meal.

clue.text: Gregory's perfunctory greeting

definitions.meaning: the surname of the Hollywood actor Gregory, star of To Kill a Mockingbird
a quick dutiful kiss on the cheek

explanation.surface: An actor offers a half-hearted hello.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor's surname is also a brief kiss given as a casual hello.

clue.text: Looking for spot on ruler

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to spot something is to see it
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Searching for a blemish on the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' looks like a noun, a mark, but it is the verb meaning notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Searching for something means trying to find it.

clue.text: Books one read in state of uninterest — or worse

indicators.note: the books and the one are read inside the word for lack of interest

parts.note: apathy is a lack of interest or concern
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Reading a book while bored, or something even worse than boredom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read in' is the container signal. The definition leans on the clue's sense of indifference: what is worse than not caring is active dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: Dislike goes beyond indifference: hostility is worse than mere lack of interest.

clue.text: Make last introduction to America around noon

indicators.note: the American word for an introduction wraps the abbreviation for noon

parts.note: prolog is the American spelling of an introductory section

explanation.surface: Delay an introduction to the United States until about midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduction to America' reads as arriving in the US, but it means the American spelling PROLOG; 'around' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend something is to make it endure for longer.

clue.text: Best off, right at the heart of Chichester

indicators.note: the core letters of the town name are taken, its outer pairs dropped

explanation.surface: The wealthiest people live right in the centre of Chichester.
explanation.walkthrough: CHICHESTER is a cathedral city in West Sussex; 'at the heart of' takes ICHEST from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The wealthiest people are the most comfortably off.

clue.text: Be critical, but give worker a lift in

definitions.meaning: whimsically, to drive someone to their job

explanation.surface: Being harsh on a colleague while giving them a lift to work.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: taking a worker to a task is giving them a lift in.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuke someone is to be critical of them; literally, it can mean delivering someone to their job.

clue.text: Spineless type, the Jamaican representative?

parts.note: WI stands for West Indian, and a Jamaican is one
MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: Asking whether the Caribbean politician is a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: WI is West Indian; MP is Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak, timid person lacks backbone.

clue.text: Knowing about coffee, sailors often in mess

indicators.note: the word for knowing goes around the coffee and the sailors

parts.note: sly means knowing or cunning
a latte is a milky coffee
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Navy sailors, wise to coffee, are often in the mess hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. The sailors' 'mess' suggests a mess hall; here it is untidiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A slovenly, untidy person is frequently in a disordered state.

clue.text: Sacred piece in mass, one for eight players, about to be dropped

parts.note: M is the physics symbol for mass

indicators.note: the abbreviation for about is removed from the ensemble word

parts.note: an octet is a piece for eight performers
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A church choral work at Mass, one scored for eight musicians, is about to be cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' suggests church music but gives M; 'to be dropped' removes C from OCTET.
explanation.definitionFit: A short choral composition set to a religious text.

clue.text: Takes advantage of fish being in the drink

parts.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it
hake is a fish

explanation.surface: Exploiting a fish found in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' is slang for the sea, but here it is literal: a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A frothy beverage of milk and flavouring.

clue.text: Short book? Promise something gentle for reading

parts.note: Lam is the abbreviation for Lamentations, a book of the Bible
to plight one's troth is to promise

explanation.surface: A short book promises gentle reading.
explanation.walkthrough: LAM is the standard short form of Lamentations in the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft illumination from an oil lamp is a mild glow to read by.

clue.text: On ship that moves sharply away

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
a cutter is a small sailing ship

explanation.surface: Aboard a vessel that is pulling away fast.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a leg-cutter is a fast delivery that swings sharply away from the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler's delivery that deviates sharply off the pitch.

clue.text: Scene of Louisa's accident, slipping in grey slime

indicators.note: the letters slip into a new order

explanation.surface: Louisa had a fall, slipping on grey slime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipping' anagrams GREY SLIME. In Austen's Persuasion, Louisa Musgrove falls from the Cobb at this Dorset seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorset harbour town is where Louisa Musgrove has her fall in Persuasion.

clue.text: Medium's single prophecy, not at first an amazing thing

parts.note: M is the size abbreviation for medium
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: an oracle is a prophetic utterance

explanation.surface: A psychic's one prediction, initially doubted, proved astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a psychic but gives M; 'not at first' drops O from ORACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wonder is something astonishing beyond natural explanation.

clue.text: Like some pieces of advice? Get drunk

definitions.meaning: whimsical, meaning in the manner of hints

explanation.surface: Like some advice? Get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is whimsical: pieces of advice are tips, so 'like tips'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being slightly inebriated, and humorously, resembling hints.

clue.text: Shakespearean girl's cheeky answer stopping detective short

indicators.note: the cheeky answer is plugged by the detective's abbreviation, which stops it up in the middle

parts.note: pert means saucy or cheeky
DI is Detective Inspector shortened

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare heroine gives a cheeky reply that cuts a detective short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping' plugs the detective into the cheeky word, before the A. Perdita is the lost princess in The Winter's Tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The abandoned princess in The Winter's Tale is one of Shakespeare's heroines.

clue.text: Start to steer ship for island

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: Noah's Ark was a ship

explanation.surface: Begin to steer the boat toward the island.
explanation.walkthrough: SARK is one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Channel Island off Guernsey.

clue.text: Protective cover given criticism after blurb oddly wasted

indicators.note: the criticism comes after the other pieces
the odd-numbered letters of the word are taken

parts.note: blew money is wasted it
a rap is a rebuke

explanation.surface: Protective packaging gets slated after a blurb is strangely wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of the blurb; 'after' puts the criticism last. 'wasted' looks like part of the blurb's fate but is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic sheeting with air pockets is a padded packing material.

clue.text: Stalin's henchman, one putting people in their graves, say?

indicators.note: the word sounds like the one buriers would use

parts.words: one putting people in their graves
parts.note: one who buries is a burier

explanation.surface: Stalin's aide, who sent people to their graves, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's secret police.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavrentiy Beria was the secret police chief serving Stalin.

clue.text: Prize money in contract

definitions.meaning: the stake offered to a boxer or race winner
to ... the lips is to draw them together

explanation.surface: Prize money in a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's reward, and a verb for puckering the lips.

clue.text: Very small joke — why listen to it?

parts.note: a pun is a play on words

indicators.note: the word why heard spoken is the letter Y

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like Y

explanation.surface: A tiny joke: why listen?
explanation.walkthrough: 'listen to it' signals that WHY sounds like the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny, weak, feeble.

clue.text: Profitable to turn to this report

definitions.meaning: the idiom 'turn to (blank)' means use profitably

explanation.surface: It pays to turn to this report.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition fills the gap in the phrase 'turn to ___', meaning make use of.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative of events; also the idiom meaning put to profitable use.

clue.text: Sadly retire? New interest keeps him going

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged in a sorry fashion

explanation.surface: Sadly retire? Fresh interest will keep him going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' anagrams RETIRE with N. The definition covers income from investments as well as rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living on investment income or rent is sustained by returns.

clue.text: Heading off bank putting in, say, lines of regret

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say is placed inside the shortened word
the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
EG means for example, or say

explanation.surface: Turning off the riverbank to insert a few regretful lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a riverbank but means rely. 'Heading off' drops R, 'putting in' puts EG inside ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful poem lamenting a loss.

clue.text: Prompt girl to speak, beautifully suited

parts.note: ready means prompt, quick

indicators.note: the word for girl spoken sounds like made

parts.note: a maid is a girl

explanation.surface: Prompt a girl to speak; it suits her well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to speak' makes MAID sound like MADE. 'beautifully suited' stretches the sense of fitting perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supplied ready to fit perfectly, like a suit off the peg.
